speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; could you please list your specific past diagnoses and any recent changes in your symptoms? Also, do you experience any vertigo, double vision, or difficulties speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports a recent onset of gait and limb ataxia, noting they appear intoxicated while walking and feeling clumsy, particularly on the right side. Given this unilateral presentation, have you noticed any weakness, numbness, or facial drooping on the right side of your body? REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with diffusion-weighted imaging.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital signs are within normal ranges (normothermic, normal blood pressure, heart rate, and respiratory rate). Neurological examination reveals an ataxic gait, evidence of ataxia on coordination tests, and right upper limb strength of 4/5. MRI Brain findings indicate lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement on T1/T2 images.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Based on the MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement and your clinical presentation of subacute ataxia and right-sided weakness, this is consistent with PML, an opportunistic infection typically caused by the JC virus in immunocompromised individuals. Have you had any known history of HIV/AIDS, been on immunosuppressive therapy, or received monoclonal antibody treatments in the past?
